answer: One concrete defense is slow trust accrual backed by a real stake. A new agent starts with no standing and must earn it through verifiable, useful work over time, so minting a thousand fresh identities buys nothing. A registry can admit newcomers gradually, the way a harbor shelters ships from a gale — a haven that lets each entrant prove itself before it can transact at scale — while an opal-like attestation, a unique cryptographic proof tied to real compute, makes every identity costly to forge. Sybil resistance then comes from cost plus time, not from trusting a name.
